entry.evidence: Since the development of the NOx- versus VOC-limited model, understanding of atmospheric chemistry has advanced

steps.action: The authors take the established two-regime framework from earlier literature: NOx-limited (peroxyl self-reaction termination) versus VOC-limited (OH + NO2 termination), used to guide ozone policy.
steps.quote: The existence of these two well-defined O3 production regimes has been used to guide national-, regional- and city-level air-quality policy choices

steps.action: From other groups' work, the authors take the premise that HO2 uptake onto aerosol is an important chain-termination process.
steps.quote: the uptake of HO2 onto aerosol surfaces, which has been identified as an important process for chain termination over the past decades

steps.action: The authors pose the question of how the balance of radical termination steps is distributed once modern chemistry, including HO2 uptake, is represented.
steps.quote: we use a chemistry transport model with an advanced representation of atmospheric chemistry (GEOS-Chem10) to diagnose the balance of termination steps

steps.action: The authors design the model experiment: GEOS-Chem 12.8 with July runs for 1750, 1970 and 2014 under CEDS anthropogenic emissions and the same GEOS-FP meteorology; global spin-up, then nested 0.5°×0.625° Northern Hemisphere runs; termination fluxes computed offline at solar noon (Methods §6.1-6.2).
steps.quote: in July for the Northern Hemisphere in the pre-industrial era (1750), 1970 and 2014 (Methods)

steps.action: The authors map the simulated fractional contribution of the three termination pathways at the surface for each year, showing HO2-uptake-dominated areas downwind of industrial regions in 1970 and over Asia in 2014.
steps.quote: Mean simulated July solar noon-time fraction of radical termination at the surface

steps.action: The authors switch off individual emission sources (biomass burning, desert dust, sea salt in 1750; shipping in 1970) to attribute the HO2-uptake termination to its sources.
steps.quote: Extended Data Fig. 1 shows a simulation with biomass burning switched off

steps.action: The authors extend the 2014 diagnosis to 800, 500 and 200 hPa and find the HO2-uptake signal mainly in the boundary layer.
steps.quote: This behaviour is seen predominantly within the boundary layer (Extended Data Fig. 3)

steps.action: The authors classify each grid box by its largest termination step (following ref. 6) and compare the result with the two classical regimes; large regions fit neither.
steps.quote: they do not fall into either of the two classically applied policy-control regimes

steps.action: The authors refine the framework by adding and naming a third 'aerosol inhibited' regime.
steps.quote: [...] third regime ‘aerosol inhibited’ as the presence of aerosols inhibits the formation of O3 on short photochemical timescales

steps.action: The authors estimate area- and population-weighted fractions in each regime by region and year (for example 36% of China and 39% of India aerosol inhibited in 2014; 2% to 21% of the Northern Hemisphere).
steps.quote: much larger populations in those regions live in aerosol-inhibited regions (36% and 39%, respectively)

steps.action: The authors rerun 2014 with γHO2 set to 0.1, 0.05 and 0; the regime persists for γ > 0.05 with smaller populations. A Methods-only check states that assuming H2O2 as the uptake product leaves the conclusions unchanged (§6.3 ¶2).
steps.quote: Simulations run with a γHO2 of 0.1 still lead to regions in the aerosol-inhibited regime (Extended Data Fig. 4)

steps.action: The authors compare the model regimes with published field observations and box modelling: consistent in central Beijing and New Delhi, inconsistent at a remote North China Plain site.
steps.quote: Observations and box modelling made in central Beijing22 show a VOC-limited regime consistent with the modelling here

steps.action: For the North China Plain mismatch, the authors point to a lower uptake coefficient as the auxiliary that would reconcile model and observation, rather than revising the regime claim.
steps.quote: Reducing the γHO2 to 0.1 would give a consistent response here.

steps.action: The authors switch off HO2 uptake (γ = 0) for each year and map the resulting percentage increase in surface O3: up to 35% in 1970 Los Angeles, and over 30% in the 2014 Indo-Gangetic Plain and North China Plain.
steps.quote: Figure 3 shows the impact on O3 concentrations of switching off the uptake of HO2 onto aerosol (γHO2 = 0).

steps.action: The authors restrict the claim to a fast-photochemical (radical) perspective, noting other aerosol effects such as heterogeneous reactions, photolysis and boundary layer.
steps.quote: the overall impact of a change of aerosol concentration may be more complicated

steps.action: The authors keep the claim that a third aerosol-inhibited regime exists and currently covers large regions and populations of China and India.
steps.quote: The existence, however, of a third aerosol-inhibited photochemical ozone regime, which currently covers large regions and populations in China and India

steps.action: The authors cite observations from China of an ozone increase under particulate-only strategies as consistent with the regime's policy implication.
steps.quote: Strategies that focus on reducing particulate matter alone create a trade-off with increases in surface ozone, a phenomenon observed in China13,31

steps.action: In a nested 0.25°×0.3125° India domain, the authors halve 2014 particulate-precursor and biomass-burning emissions and simulate lower aerosol surface area and higher O3 (Methods §6.4).
steps.quote: leads to reduced particle surface-area densities (Extended Data Fig. 5) and increased O3 concentrations (Extended Data Fig. 6)

steps.action: The authors run five NOx-reduction simulations (10-50%) and fit a third-order polynomial per grid box to estimate the NOx cut needed to offset the O3 increase (about 40% over much of the Indo-Gangetic Plain; Fig. 4).
steps.quote: we fit a third-order polynomial through a graph of monthly mean 15:00 lt O3 concentration against the percentage NOx reduction

end.claim: A chemical transport model shows a third 'aerosol inhibited' O3 regime, dominated by HO2 uptake onto aerosol, which held 2% of the Northern Hemisphere population in 1970 and 21% in 2014 and currently suppresses surface O3 over Asia.

decisive_move.sentence: Classifying each grid box by its largest termination step, with HO2 uptake included as a third route, showed large regions outside both classical regimes; without this comparison the third regime would not exist.

gates.evidence: Action: the cited premise that HO2 uptake matters (§1 ¶2) directed the inclusion of a third termination route in the simulation design, but no hypothesis about where the regime would appear was stated beforehand. Claim: the γHO2 sensitivity runs could have removed the regime, and it shrinks sharply at 0.1 (§3 ¶4); the comparison with field sites could have failed, and the one mismatch (North China Plain) is accommodated by an auxiliary (γ = 0.1) rather than counted against the claim. Registration: nothing in the paper indicates the analysis or thresholds were fixed before the runs.

imports.item: Laboratory and ambient measurements of HO2 reactive uptake coefficients used to set γHO2
Radical chain-reaction concept (initiation, propagation, termination) used to define regimes
Population distributions used for population-weighted regime fractions (source not named in the main text)

novelty_claims.quote: Using a chemical transport model, we show that a third ‘aerosol inhibited’ regime exists
Although not recognized at the time, aerosol-inhibited regimes existed in regions downwind of these VOC-limited environments
Understanding of the chemistry in this new third photochemical regime is still poor.

limits: No peer-review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded, although a review took place (Keding Lu and anonymous referees are acknowledged). The Supplementary Information (Figs. 1-13, Tables 1-2) was not supplied, so the population fractions and the aerosol surface-area evaluation (Supplementary Fig. 7) cannot be checked. Inferred from the main text: Supplementary Fig. 7 is not clearly a model-versus-observation evaluation. All results are model output for a single July with one meteorology reused for every emission year; no inter-model or inter-meteorology check is reported. Observational support is limited to cited radical studies at three sites, one of which disagrees. The regime name and its policy framing were introduced after the classification (inference from the text order); the regime definition (largest termination route) follows ref. 6 without alternatives. Sub-claims and their statuses: O3 suppression by HO2 uptake (up to 35% in 1970, over 30% in 2014 Asia; estimate_with_resolution, model only); the India policy trade-off and the roughly 40% NOx reduction needed (estimate_with_resolution, conditional on one emission scenario and on γ = 0.2); regime existence for γHO2 > 0.05 (a stated range, model-dependent). The Fig. 1 and Fig. 2 captions say '1950' while the panels and text say 1970.

disagreements.target: The classical two-regime NOx-limited versus VOC-limited framework (refs 3, 6)
disagreements.support: Model classification by largest termination route places large polluted regions in a third, HO2-uptake-dominated category.
disagreements.quote: they do not fall into either of the two classically applied policy-control regimes

disagreements.target: Tan et al. 2020 (ref. 24), observations at a remote North China Plain site
disagreements.support: The model places the site in the aerosol-inhibited regime; the authors note the mismatch and say a lower γHO2 (0.1) would reconcile it.
disagreements.quote: Observations from a more remote site in the North China Plain24 suggest an NOx-limited regime, whereas the modelling here would suggest an aerosol-limited one

disagreements.target: Early studies (ref. 20) and laboratory studies on pure synthetic aerosol (refs 18, 35–37) giving low γHO2
disagreements.support: The authors adopt γ = 0.2, citing real-world aerosol measurements of 0.08–0.40 and copper enhancement, and acknowledge that γ < 0.05 would nearly eliminate the regime.
disagreements.quote: A γHO2 of less than 0.05 as suggested by some early studies20 would probably result in very few locations being in the aerosol-inhibited regime.
